tooltip.refineddelight.bound: Bound to the Refined Storage network
A Farmer's Delight cooking pot that draws its ingredients from a Refined Storage network. It still needs a heat source beneath it to cook.

Bind it with sneak + right-click on any block of your Refined Storage network. The network needs a Wireless Transmitter in range for the pot to connect. Pick a recipe from the panel and the pot pulls everything it needs — from your inventory first, then the network.

Meals stay in the pot until you give it serving containers, by hand or with the request button. Only items pulled from the network cost battery. Charge the battery from any FE source, or with an energy cable against a placed pot's side.

entry.refineddelight.wireless_cooking_po: The $(item)Wireless Cooking Pot$() is a Farmer's Delight cooking pot that can reach into a Refined Storage network for its ingredients.$(br2)It is still a cooking pot: it needs a $(thing)heat source$() beneath it, and it cooks the same recipes at the same speed.
Crafted from a cooking pot and the parts of a Wireless Grid.

Hold the pot and $(thing)sneak + right-click$() any block of your Refined Storage network — the controller, a cable, any device. That only tells the pot $(o)which network$() to use, so pick something that will stay put.$(br2)You must sneak: a plain right-click opens that block's own screen instead.$(br2)To actually connect, the network needs a $(thing)Wireless Transmitter$() whose range covers the pot. Range and dimension are the transmitter's business, not the pot's: fit it with $(thing)range upgrades$() and the pot reaches exactly as far as any other wireless device on that network.

Load ingredients by hand and it behaves exactly like the vanilla pot.$(br2)Or open the $(thing)recipe panel$() and click a recipe: the pot pulls a single serving. $(thing)Shift-click$() pulls as many as it can hold at once.$(br2)Ingredients come from $(o)your inventory first$(), then the network.

Cooked meals collect inside the pot — up to $(thing)64$(), however small the meal's own stack size.$(br2)They only come out when the recipe's $(thing)serving container$() is provided: place bowls or bottles in the container slot, or press the $(thing)request$() button to pull them from the network.$(br2)Break the pot and any waiting meal travels inside it.

The pot carries its own battery, charged from any $(thing)Forge Energy$() source, including an $(thing)energy cable$() run into the side of a placed pot.$(br2)It pays for $(o)network access only$(): items taken from your own inventory are free, and cooking itself costs nothing. Holding the link open draws a small idle trickle.$(br2)The battery and the binding both survive breaking and replacing the pot.
